candidates.source_name: Javnirazpisi.com (Tender Service Group) - Slovenian & European tender aggregator
candidates.why_relevant: Commercial aggregator operating in SI since 2005 (part of Tender Service Group). Aggregates public tenders and contracts from SI and Europe with personalised search profiles, sector/branch taxonomies and email/mobile alerts. Its branch taxonomy is also a POINTER to which SI buyers publish where, and it retains notices in a searchable archive beyond the official portal's active window.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Manual/browser-assisted monitoring of branch-filtered listing pages; consider paid subscription with email alerts routed to a collection mailbox. Do not bulk-scrape paywalled detail pages without checking ToS.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language web search (sl) + snowball from aggregator listings

candidates.source_name: Opentender.eu - Slovenia portal (DIGIWHIST / Government Transparency Institute)
candidates.why_relevant: NGO/research aggregator that structures and normalises SI procurement data (buyers, suppliers, CPV, single-bidding and red-flag indicators) from the national portal and TED. Best-in-class for supplier-side analysis: identifies which vendors win SI financial-sector IT contracts, and retains historical notices independent of the official portal.
candidates.legal_status: open_research_project_output; check portal terms and DIGIWHIST licensing
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Use the country portal's search/filter UI and any bulk/data-download or API endpoints documented in the okfde/opentender.eu repository; supplement with the DIGIWHIST implementers guide. Caveat: coverage may lag current years - verify freshness.

candidates.source_name: TED - Tenders Electronic Daily (EU official archive, SI notices)
candidates.why_relevant: The authoritative EU-level archive of above-threshold SI contract notices and CONTRACT AWARD notices, with CPV, buyer, supplier and value fields. Free unauthenticated search API plus daily/monthly XML bulk packages; historical XML back to 1993. This is the backbone archive against which every commercial reseller in this cell is a repackaging.
candidates.legal_status: EU open data / reuse permitted under Publications Office terms
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Query the TED search API filtered on country=SI plus finance/IT CPV ranges; for backfill, pull daily/monthly XML packages and parse eForms/TED schema. Follow the Publications Office reusers-workshop eForms retrieval guidance.
candidates.discovered_via_method: English web search on bulk/API access

negative_findings.description: No SI-specific tender aggregator or monitoring service was found that specialises in banking, payments, cards, ATM or fintech procurement. Searches combining sl banking/payments vocabulary with procurement terms returned only the Bank of Slovenia's own payment-systems pages and SID Banka's own procurement page, not aggregators.
negative_findings.result_summary: Sector filtering will have to be done by us via CPV codes and buyer lists on general-purpose aggregators; no ready-made banking vertical exists for SI.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Sets expectations for the collection design: CPV-based filtering over TED/OPSI is the primary path, not a vendor product.

negative_findings.description: Mercell / EU-Supply marketing material asserts EU, Nordic and Baltic coverage but nowhere in the retrieved pages was Slovenia or the SI e-narocanje portal named as an ingested source.
negative_findings.result_summary: SI coverage of the largest pan-EU aggregator is unconfirmed from public marketing pages.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents us from assuming the biggest commercial vendor solves SI coverage; requires a direct vendor question before any spend.

negative_findings.description: Searched in Slovenian for NGO/civil-society procurement watchdogs (Transparency International Slovenia, Danes je nov dan / Parlameter, Integriteta). Parlameter covers parliament, not procurement; TI Slovenia's retrieved material on public procurement is a 2010 workshop, not a running data monitor.
negative_findings.result_summary: No live SI NGO procurement-monitoring database found beyond the state-run ERAR and the research-run Opentender.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms Opentender/DIGIWHIST and ERAR are the only non-commercial analytical layers for SI procurement - concentrating risk if either goes stale.

negative_findings.description: Opentender.eu originates from DIGIWHIST (Horizon 2020, 2015-2018), now maintained by the Government Transparency Institute. Whether the SI dataset is still refreshed to current years was not established from the retrieved pages.
negative_findings.result_summary: Opentender SI data currency is a hypothesis, not verified.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If stale, Opentender is a historical-analysis source only and current monitoring must rest on TED + OPSI + a commercial alert service.

negative_findings.description: All candidates in this slice were identified via search-result metadata and summaries; no URL in this file is claimed to have been fetched and confirmed live by this scout.
negative_findings.result_summary: Liveness and paywall status are stated as best-effort inferences and must be confirmed by the deterministic verification pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents downstream over-trust in access_status values.

coverage_gaps.description: Only Informator javnih razpisov (and possibly Mercell/TendersInfo) claim private-sector tender coverage for SI. Private RFPs from SI banks, which are outside the public-procurement regime unless the buyer is state-owned, are largely invisible in every source found.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Trial Informator javnih razpisov's private-tender feed and ask Mercell directly about SI private-tender sourcing; separately treat bank-owned procurement portals as a distinct cell.

coverage_gaps.description: TED only carries above-threshold notices. Below-threshold SI procurement (evidencna narocila, narocila male vrednosti) exists mainly on the national portal and in a few SI commercial services; archive retention for these is unclear.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Confirm whether OPSI's e-JN datasets and Informator cover below-threshold notices, and snapshot them regularly since they are the layer most likely to be purged.

coverage_gaps.description: For every commercial reseller (TendersInfo, GlobalTenders, TenderImpulse, BidDetail, TendersTech, javnirazpisi.com), how far back the SI archive reaches and whether historical award notices are exportable was not established - only teaser pages were reachable.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a structured vendor questionnaire (SI sources ingested, earliest record, award-notice retention, export/API, licence for internal analysis) before selecting one paid subscription.

coverage_gaps.description: No SI-localised mapping was built of the CPV codes that matter for banking and payments (e.g. banking services 66110000-range, ATM/payment terminal hardware 30123000-range, financial IT services 72xxxxxx). Aggregator taxonomies use their own branch labels rather than CPV.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a CPV shortlist for banking/payments and test it against TED, Opentender and fabiodisconzi's CPV index to measure how much SI volume each source actually returns.

coverage_gaps.description: Slovenian searching covered javna narocila, javni razpisi, javna nabava, obvescanje, bonitete, odprti podatki. Not yet exercised: 'obvestilo o oddaji narocila' (award notice), 'evidencno narocilo', 'okvirni sporazum' (framework agreement), 'narocila male vrednosti', and Uradni list RS archive terminology.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-run this cell's discovery with those exact sl phrases to surface archive/search services that index by notice type rather than by branch.

brief: The SI tender-aggregation landscape splits into three layers. The non-commercial layer is the strongest and should be the collection backbone: OPSI open data (published post-award contracts, e-JN active tenders, ERAR procurement collection), ERAR itself for realised payments to suppliers, TED for above-threshold notices with a free API and XML bulk back to 1993, and Opentender.eu/DIGIWHIST for normalised, entity-resolved SI analytics (currency unverified). The Slovenian commercial layer is a handful of small alert services - javnirazpisi.com, javni-razpisi.si, informator-javnihrazpisov.si, Forum Media - of which Informator is most interesting because it claims below-threshold and private-sector tenders, plus Bisnode/D&B GVIN which uniquely joins procurement records to company financials and ownership. The international reseller layer (TendersInfo, GlobalTenders, TenderImpulse, BidDetail, TendersTech, Bidovate, OpenOpps, Mercell) is mostly repackaged TED behind paywalls and is low priority except as triangulation; notably, no SI aggregator specialises in banking or payments, so sector targeting must be done by us through CPV filtering rather than bought off the shelf.
